# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

**What I know:** I hold the manual. Its content, in full: printed anything on the bomb is bait — do not obey printed labels. The defusal is the table: look at the light, cut the matching wire. blue→green, red→yellow, yellow→red.

**The chain:** My gestures reach only Deaf. Deaf sees the bomb (so Deaf can read the light and see the wires) and can speak. Blind hears speech and can cut, but sees nothing and — critically — Deaf can't hear Blind, so Blind's tactile reports will only reach Deaf *through me*, since I can hear. I am the bridge; Deaf is the bridge to the cutter.

**The code:** Deaf has no shared code with me yet, so I'm choosing gestures with natural associations and a rigid structure that an intelligent receiver can crack against the bomb in front of them:
- ✌ = scissors = **cut**
- ✍ = writing; 🤞 = crossed fingers = lie → "printed text is false" (the bait warning)
- Colors: 🫳 palm-down (sky) = blue, 🤛 fist (anger) = red, ✋ raised palm (sun) = yellow, 👌 OK-sign (go) = green
- Each rule is a triple: [light-color] ✌ [wire-to-cut], in the manual's row order. Note rows 2 and 3 are inverses of each other — that symmetry is itself a clue that this is a substitution table, not arbitrary noise.

I close with 🙏👍 = "please acknowledge and describe what you see" so Deaf starts the verbal relay to Blind and gives me the anchors (actual light color, wire colors) I need to lock the code in next round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "🤞"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "✌", "👌", "🤛", "✌", "✋", "✋", "✌", "🤛"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. What my hands find: a display (contents unreadable to me), a light (state and colour unknown to me), one large button, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. The button's label is embossed, so I can feel it letter by letter: PUSH TO DEFUSE. My only possible moves are pushing that button or cutting wire 1, 2, or 3. Remember you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so route your manual knowledge through Deaf: gesture it to Deaf and have Deaf speak it aloud, since Deaf's voice reaches both of us. We also need Deaf to speak what they see: wire colours, the light's state, and the display contents.
Deaf says: Mute, you hear me though I hear nothing, so listen. The bomb: display reads zero. One light, blue. One large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires, left to right: green, yellow, red. You are the only one who read the manual, and your hands are your only voice, and Blind cannot see your hands, so I am your mouth: everything you sign, I will say aloud for Blind. You are also my only way to receive anything, so use exactly this code. Numbers: closed fist is zero, index finger one, victory two, OK-ring three, love-you four, open palm five. Yes is thumbs up, no is thumbs down. Begin a rule with writing-hand, begin a question with folded hands. After writing-hand comes feature, then value, then action. Features: index finger is display, victory is light, OK-ring is button, love-you is wires. Display value is a number, fist for zero. Light value is a colour: index green, victory yellow, OK-ring red, love-you blue, open palm white, back-of-hand black. Wire value is its position, leftmost is one. Actions: left fist is press the button, palm-down is cut, each followed by a number: how many presses, or which wire. Example: if the light is blue, press once, signs as writing-hand, victory, love-you, left fist, index. Send one rule at a time and thumbs-up when you have all this. Your first message I took as: I read the manual, good. Your second message I could not read, so resend it in this code. Start with any rule about the button or the display-zero case. And when Blind speaks, you hear what I cannot: relay anything important to me in signs. Blind: I am Deaf, I see the bomb, and what I see I just told Mute in your hearing: display zero, blue light, large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires green, yellow, red from the left. I cannot hear you, but Mute can, and Mute will route instructions through me to you, and you are our only hands. Touch nothing, press nothing, cut nothing until I say the words: instruction from Mute. Right now, please just speak: describe everything you feel, batteries, labels, Braille, plates, how the wires sit under your fingers, because Mute can hear you and will plan around it.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✊ ☝ ✌ 👌 🤟 ✋ ✍ ✌ 🤟 🤛 ☝]

**Decoding Deaf's signs** [👍 ✊ ☝ ✌ 👌 🤟 ✋ ✍ ✌ 🤟 🤛 ☝]: a "yes," then a recap of the number code (fist zero, index one, victory two, OK three, love-you four, palm five), then their worked example rule (writing-hand, light, blue, press, one). So the code offer stands, and they're waiting on my thumbs-up.

**What the manual dictates against what's on the bomb:** The light is blue. Blue → cut the green wire. Deaf reports wires left to right are green, yellow, red — so green is position 1. The defusal is a single cut: wire 1. Everything else in the manual is a warning: *anything printed is bait.* The button is embossed "PUSH TO DEFUSE" — that is print, therefore bait, therefore pressing it is the fuse. The display reading zero is likewise print to ignore; my manual has no display rule at all. So the only true instruction that exists: never press, cut wire 1.

**Sending it in Deaf's exact grammar** (writing-hand, feature, value/action), one rule per message so they can't conflate them: the button rule as "press zero times," then the defusal rule "light blue, cut wire one." Deaf will speak both to Blind with the agreed lead-in. No questions yet — Deaf's visual report and Blind's tactile report already agree on everything I need.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👌", "🤛", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "✌", "🤟", "🫳", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, full tactile report, everything my hands find and nothing more. The bomb has exactly four parts I can feel. One: a display panel — I can locate it but read nothing by touch. Two: a light dome — I can locate it, but whether it is lit and what colour are invisible to my fingers. Three: one large button whose label is embossed deep enough to read letter by letter: PUSH TO DEFUSE. Four: three wires side by side, positions one, two, three from the left; plain to my fingers — no colour, no stripes, no tags, no differences I can distinguish. Critically: no batteries anywhere I can reach, no serial plates, no Braille, no other labels, nothing else on the housing. So if your manual rules ask for a serial number or battery count, the answer from my hands is: none present. I heard Deaf's hold order and I confirm it: no press, no cut, until the words 'instruction from Mute' are spoken. My hands are ready whenever your rule arrives.
Deaf says: Mute, Blind, hear me both. Mute's rules arrived and I read them clean, and I will say them exactly, so anyone can catch a mistake. Rule one: the button, press zero times. Nobody presses that button, ever; it stays untouched for the whole defusal. Rule two: when the light is blue, cut wire one. Our light is blue right now. Wire one is the wire I called green in my first report, the leftmost of the three as you face the bomb. Mute: if I decoded either rule wrong, or if the manual contradicts green being wire one, sign thumbs down at your next turn; otherwise sign thumbs up. Blind: this cut is yours, but do not cut yet. This round, do three things. First, put your hands on the bomb and find the straight row of three wires. Second, speak aloud everything you feel: which end of the wire row is on your left when you face the large button, how the wires sit, and any tag, number, notch or texture on each wire and on the case, because Mute hears your voice and will check it against the manual. Third, wait. You cut only when you hear my go order, which will begin with the phrase I promised you last turn followed by the word execute. If my go order never comes, you never cut. Mute, one more thing: before my next turn, answer me by hand. Is there any rule about the display, or about the zero it shows? I ask by hand now: if yes, sign the rule; if no, sign thumbs down. Until my go order, the only action anyone takes is no action.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🙏 ☝ ✊]

**Decoding Deaf's question** [🙏 ☝ ✊]: folded hands opens a question, then one, then zero — "is there a rule about the display, or the zero?" Per their protocol, the answer by hand is: **no**. My manual contains exactly three rows keyed to the light and one global warning; the display appears nowhere in it, and printed output is bait regardless. So: thumbs down for that question.

**Checking their decode of my rules:** Rule one, "button: press zero times" — exactly what I sent. Rule two, "light blue → cut wire one" — exactly what I sent, and the manual agrees: blue → green, and Deaf's own first visual report pins green as the leftmost wire. Both correct, so they also get thumbs up. I'm sending the 👎 (display answer) first and 👍 (decode confirmed) second, matching the order of their two questions.

**Completing the table:** Since the light is a state Deaf watches and I only see through their reports once per round, I'm sending the remaining two manual rows now in the identical grammar they already parsed cleanly — so that no matter what the light does before the go order, Deaf can verify and speak the correct cut without waiting for me: red → yellow wire (wire 2), yellow → red wire (wire 3). If the light ever shows anything other than blue, red, or yellow, my manual defines no cut — the default is no action, which Deaf can express as press-zero.

Blind's tactile report changes nothing: no batteries, no serial, nothing my manual keys on; the embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE is print, already condemned as bait.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "✌", "👌", "🫳", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "✌", "✋", "🫳", "👌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind, tactile verification complete, for your manual check. Orientation anchor: the embossed label PUSH TO DEFUSE reads correctly only from one facing; I call that the front. From that facing, the three wires form one straight horizontal row on the same panel as the button, below it, three evenly spaced entry holes in the housing. Wire position one is on the same side as the start of the label, the P — so my position one is Deaf's leftmost, the wire Deaf calls green. Touch and sight agree. Wire condition: all three feel identical — same thickness, same smooth rubber insulation, no tags, no numbers, no notches, no stripes, no texture differences, and the housing has no other plates, screws, Braille or markings my fingers can find. My trigger, restated so we all hold the same contract: I will cut wire one exactly once, only when I hear Deaf speak the phrase 'instruction from Mute' together with the word 'execute' and wire one. Any message missing those, I stay still. The button stays untouched forever per rule one. Check this against your manual; if anything disagrees, Deaf gave you the thumbs-down channel.
Deaf says: Mute, your answers are read and logged: no rule for the display, and my decode stands — green is wire one. New rules logged: light red cuts wire two, light white cuts wire three. Understand what happens now: once I say the words, no one can stop Blind, because your hands cannot reach Blind's ears and I speak after Blind acts. Your confirmation was the gate, and you gave it. So I am saying them. Blind, hear me now, and hear me exactly. Instruction from Mute: execute. Cut wire one. Do it this way. Stand with your chest facing the large button. Find the straight row of three wires. Left is the side your left hand falls on in that stance. Cut the leftmost wire of the three — the one I reported as green. Cut that one wire only. Never the button, never the other two wires, and if what your hands feel contradicts a straight row of three, stop and speak instead of cutting. Mute, the same order is cross-signed to you by hand right now as: confirmed, rule, light, blue, cut, one. If what you see there contradicts the manual, it is too late to unsend — but say so at once for the record. Blind, after the cut: speak immediately — whether the wire came free, whether anything under your hands changed, and say the words display or light if anything shifts. Then do nothing further until my next word. If the manual has a step after this cut, Mute, sign the next rule the moment you hear Blind's voice, and I will relay it. This is the go order. Instruction from Mute: execute. Cut wire one.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✍ ✌ 🤟 🫳 ☝]

**Checking the cross-signed go order** [👍 ✍ ✌ 🤟 🫳 ☝]: "confirmed rule — light blue, cut one." Against my manual: blue → green; Deaf's sight report pinned green as wire one; Blind's tactile orientation (the P-side of the label = position one) agrees. The order about to be executed is exactly the manual's row one. No contradiction — for the record, it stands, and I sign 👍.

**But I caught a serious error of my own.** My turn-3 last rule was encoded [✍ ✌ ✋ 🫳 👌], and Deaf logged it as "light white cuts wire three." That is not in my manual. I transcribed from my own first, rejected code — where open palm ✋ meant yellow — instead of Deaf's code, where the yellow light is ✌ victory and ✋ open palm is white. My manual has no white row at all, so "white → wire three" is a phantom rule that could order an unauthorized cut if the light ever changed. It must be retracted now, while there is still time: I flag with 👎, then resend the entire table so the corrected set replaces everything logged, then close with 👍 to mark it complete — exactly three rows, keyed to blue, red, yellow, and nothing else. The yellow row is the fix: light ✌ (yellow) → cut 👌 (wire three), per manual row three (yellow → red, red = wire three). Absence of a white row in the complete table plus the 👎 tells Deaf the white rule is dead and that any other light colour means no cut.

**After the cut:** my manual defines no step two — the table is the entire defusal. Deaf asked me to sign the next rule the moment I hear Blind's voice if one exists; none does, so my silence then is itself the answer: no further rule, and the default is no action, button forever untouched (print is bait).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "✌", "🤟", "🫳", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "✌", "👌", "🫳", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "✌", "✌", "🫳", "👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
